sentences.text: Tubonasus is an extinct genus of long-snouted arthrodire placoderm known only from one species.
This fish possessed an elongated rostrum, a streamlined body, and narrow infragnathals.
The genus Tubonasus was described by Dennis and Miles in 1979.
Researchers interpret Tubonasus as a pelagic pursuit predator capable of swallowing prey whole.
Tubonasus belongs to the family Camuropiscidae, the superfamily Incisoscutoidea, and the clade Coccosteomorphi.
Tubonasus is classified within the class Placodermi.
Tubonasus lived during the Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.
Fossils of Tubonasus date from 382.31 to 379 million years ago.
Tubonasus fossils have been found in the Gogo Formation of Kimberley, Western Australia.
